summary.headline: Star Cement Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR164 crores (from INR194 crores) and PAT to INR39.58 crores, with management guiding 12-13% H2 volume growth.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 cement volumes rose to 11.23 lakh tons from 10.72 lakh tons, but EBITDA fell about 15% YoY to INR164 crores and per-ton EBITDA dropped to INR1,372 from INR1,651. Q2 demand was hit by Assam floods, elections and Manipur unrest, while October sales were reportedly above 12% growth. Management kept the FY27 EBITDA guidance, reiterated a 7-8% full-year volume outlook, and said the Nimbol clinker and grinding project (ground-breaking from 1 December) and the Jhajjar grinding unit are on track. Capex phasing for FY28 was raised to about INR1,900 crores, with the timing flagged as flexible.

segments.name: Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Q2 sales were 7.96 lakh tons vs 7.84 lakh tons last year. Management said Assam and Nagaland flooding and Manipur unrest drove a roughly 25% decline in those markets. Trade share was 77%.

segments.name: Outside Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Q2 sales were 3.27 lakh tons vs 2.88 lakh tons last year, with West Bengal growth in the higher teens expected for H2. Blend was about 18% OPC and the rest PPC.

segments.name: Clinker sales
segments.commentary: Q2 clinker sales were 0.74 lakh tons vs 1.01 lakh tons last year, and H1 clinker sales were about 1.26 lakh tons. Management said clinker tonnage will fall from Q3 as prices are raised to sell selectively.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit H2 volume growth, with about 12-13% YoY company volume growth in Q3 and Q4 and October above 12%.
Full-year 7-8% cement volume growth target is said to remain intact.
FY27 EBITDA guidance is reaffirmed, though the specific figure was not restated on the call; an analyst cited INR1,500-1,600 crores.
Assam Norway (incentive) subsidy accrual is expected at about INR65-70 crores in H2 after the scheme change; H1 subsidy booked was about INR60 crores.
Fuel cost is guided to about INR1.5 per kcal through Q3 and Q4, with management targeting INR1.45 by end-March.
Target of about 20 million tons capacity by 2030-31, with about 18 million tons expected in roughly two years.
capex_capacity: Nimbol (Rajasthan) expansion is now 6 million tons (up from 5 million): 3.3 million tons clinker rated (about 3.6 million tons at full capacity) and 3 million tons cement grinding. EC is expected within a week or two, and ground-breaking starts 1 December 2026, with commissioning around July-August 2028.

Jhajjar grinding unit is 3 million tons (up from 2 million). About 50 acres of land is aggregated, with clarity expected in about a month, and it is expected to commission in the same quarter as Nimbol clinker.

Second eastern grinding unit (2 million tons): Siliguri (West Bengal) is estimated at about INR350 crores capex, vs Bihar at about INR550 crores. EC has been applied for in Siliguri, and the decision is expected in the next call.

Capex guidance (Q1 deck): about INR560 crores in FY27, about INR1,910 crores in FY28 and INR610 crores in FY29. H1 FY27 capex spend was about INR203 crores. Management said the figures are flexible and can shift between FY28, FY29 and FY30 via buyer's credit.

Umrangso (Northeast) clinker plant: EC ToR received, EC expected in 2-3 months, plant land acquired, and the project can be commissioned in about 18-20 months once triggered. The decision depends on demand.
Silchar: power connection partly done; railway siding expected by January 2027, which should lower fly ash costs and improve plant economics from Q4.
demand_pricing: Northeast pricing was broadly flat in September and rose about INR10 per bag in October in Northeast, with INR10-15 outside Northeast (including West Bengal). Management said the increase outside Northeast is weaker.

Competitive threat: JK Lakshmi, Ambuja (4 million tons) and Shree Cement are planning Northeast capacity. Management expects 2-2.5 years for kilns to come up, a 1 million ton kiln each for Shree and JK Lakshmi, and short-term price pressure.
Outside-Northeast cement, about 15-16% of Northeast market (about 2.4-2.5 million tons per year), comes via rakes from Chhattisgarh and West Bengal on consignment.
Premium share 17.3%, lead distance 208 km, clinker factor 68.6%, green power 28%.

Fuel mix in Q2: FSA about 45%, washery and coke fine coal about 40%, biomass about 11.5%, spot auction coal about 10%. About three months of coal stock is held. Coal India FSA deliveries resumed in November (about five rakes so far, with about 60 rakes pending).
Incentive: Nimbol and Northeast incentive structure is expected to be similar in quantum, though new schemes allow about 110% of fixed capital investment vs about 200% under the existing scheme.

qa_highlights.question: How will H2 volumes shape up and how was October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects double-digit H2 growth, with about 12-13% YoY in Q3 and Q4. October growth was above 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fuel cost stay flat at INR1.55 vs the guided INR1.45 in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 was INR1.52 and that AFR availability was constrained in the rains. Fuel is guided to about INR1.5 for Q3 and Q4, with INR1.45 targeted by end-March.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Nimbol EC come through and when does ground-breaking start?
qa_highlights.answer: The EAC meeting was successful, the EC is expected to be granted in a week or two, and ground-breaking is planned for 1 December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will the QIP be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the stance of net debt to EBITDA staying below 1.5x holds for now, and capex will be funded through debt and internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Why was clinker sold in H1, and how will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Clinker is sold to non-branded grinders, with some going to Siliguri and Nepal. Prices were raised from Q3, so tonnage will fall but margins are expected to improve.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Northeast price outlook secure given new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects short-term price pressure but long-term stability, since the market is about 1.5 million tons per year of growth, and the incumbents retain trade dominance.

risks_watch: Coal supply: FSA deliveries were absent through September and October, with about 60 rakes pending. Industry fuel prices are rising above INR2 per kcal, which could cut margins if the guided INR1.5 is missed.
Northeast competition: JK Lakshmi, Ambuja and Shree Cement capacity could pressure prices, and out-of-region rake supply (15-16% share) is a swing factor.
Capex and timing: FY28 capex outlay is about INR1,910 crores, and Bihar vs Siliguri and Jhajjar land and EC clarity are pending. The Q2 deck update is due in about a week.
Manipur unrest and Assam flooding have hurt Northeast demand, and H2 relies on about 12-13% company growth against a 7-8% industry growth outlook.
Non-cement and incentive income: Assam incentive accruals (H2 about INR65-70 crores) are a material part of profit. The power cost per unit was not disclosed on the call.
Q2 EBITDA and per-ton EBITDA declined sharply YoY, so the reaffirmed FY27 EBITDA guidance needs H2 recovery.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume recovery and the Nimbol project timeline, but cautious on Northeast pricing and the coal supply outlook. Management was less precise on capex phasing and Bihar vs Siliguri, and deferred some data requests.
key_quotes: We do expect double-digit growth in the second half, in terms of volume.
The money in Northeast is not in asset turnover; it is in margin.
We are starting our ground-breaking from 1st of December in Nimbol.
I think in the next three months, the panic around coal prices should reduce because the FSAs will start delivering.

growth.why: Management reiterated 7-8% FY27 volume growth and 12-13% YoY volume growth in Q3 and Q4 (October above 12%), with H1 volumes up only about 5% and the Nimbol/Jhajjar capacity not live until roughly 2028, so H2 growth rests mainly on demand recovery post-floods and elections rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 per-ton EBITDA fell to INR1,372 from INR1,651, but management guides fuel to about INR1.5/kcal in Q3-Q4 (INR1.45 by end-March), a price rise from Q3, and H2 Assam subsidy accrual of INR65-70 crores, against FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR1,500-1,600 per ton.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Nimbol 6 Mt expansion (3.3 Mt clinker, 3 Mt grinding) has ground-breaking from 1 Dec 2026 with commissioning around July-August 2028, but none of the new capacity is live in the H2 FY27 window, so the window carries no new volume.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided 12-13% YoY volume growth in Q3 and Q4 with October above 12%, versus H1 volumes up only about 5% and Q2 at 11.23 lakh tons vs 10.72 lakh tons, though Northeast demand fell about 25% in flood-hit markets.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is high (11.56 lakh tons produced in Q2 vs 10.83 lakh tons last year), and the Siliguri EC decision and Jhajjar land clarity (about a month) are pending, so further capex approvals are likely in the window.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA guidance was only reaffirmed after a 15% YoY EBITDA decline in Q2 (INR164 crores vs INR194 crores), and management is relying on H2 recovery without a raise signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA fell to INR164 crores from INR194 crores, coal FSA deliveries were absent through September and October (about 60 rakes pending), and industry fuel is above INR2/kcal against the guided INR1.5, so a miss on the FY27 EBITDA target is a live risk.

rows.label: Northeast competitive entry (JK Lakshmi, Ambuja, Shree)
rows.why: Kilns from Shree and JK Lakshmi (1 Mt each) and Ambuja (4 Mt) are planned for the Northeast, and management expects short-term price pressure before the new kilns arrive in about 2-2.5 years.

rows.label: Northeast price increase from October
rows.why: Northeast prices rose about INR10 per bag in October and INR10-15 outside the Northeast, but management says the increase outside the Northeast is weaker and short-term price pressure is expected.

rows.label: No QIP; debt-funded capex
rows.why: Management said the net debt/EBITDA stance of below 1.5x holds, with capex funded through debt and internal accruals and no QIP planned.

tone.note: Management was confident on the H2 volume recovery and the Nimbol timeline, but cautious on Northeast pricing, competition and coal supply, and less precise on capex phasing and Bihar vs Siliguri; analysts pushed on the Q2 EBITDA decline and fuel cost miss.
